headline: Microsoft says Windows will run AI agents on the PC or in the cloud and is bringing open models such as DeepSeek and Nvidia's Nemotron to the PC.
score_reason: Pool score 5 kept: a platform plan from a major company; the rollout is slow and the speed figures are the companies' own tests.
importance_line: PC users and businesses get more control over what AI agents can reach, but the honest doubt is that features arrive slowly with no set dates per country, and the speed figures come from tests run by Microsoft and Nvidia.
summary: trendingtopics.eu reports, drawing on Microsoft's announcement, that Windows is being built as a 'hybrid intelligence' platform where AI agents run on the PC or in the cloud, and that open-weight models (AI models that anyone can download) are coming to the PC, including DeepSeek and Nemotron. Microsoft says its sandboxes, which limit which files and networks an AI agent can reach, are now generally available on Windows 11, while new Copilot features are coming only to Copilot+ PCs over the coming months.
notes: Read in full from trendingtopics.eu (6,975 chars); German boilerplate ignored. The article's citations to Tom's Hardware and Windows Central were not read.
